clue.text: Attend a soldier's party and make a run for it

parts.note: to attend is to be present, split here as BE AT
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers; the 's is read as 'is'
a treat is an outing or party laid on for someone

explanation.surface: Someone goes to an army knees-up and then bolts from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the name of a military ceremony with drums, which makes 'soldier's party' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to beat a retreat is to withdraw hastily, much as one flees or bolts.

clue.text: Senior officer to fix promotion during last stand

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: a bier is the stand on which a coffin rests, the last one anyone needs
to rig is to fix a result dishonestly
AD is short for advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A senior officer rigs his own promotion during a desperate last stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last stand' suggests a final battle; here it is the bier for a coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym by rank: a brigadier is a high-ranking army officer commanding a brigade.

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it, so the outer word holds the inner one

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek suffers aches and illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad, a legendary warrior of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Mark tucks into a scotch — that's better

indicators.note: one piece tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a glass of Scotch whisky and feels better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it is the verb meaning stop or end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to improve a text or law by correcting it is to make it better.

definitions.note: a phrase for a place, standing for a city located there

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bride hangs about on her wedding day somewhere north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only a location; the answer is the capital city, found in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital city of Scotland, a place lying in that country.

indicators.note: placed in the other word, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: rule is power or control over a country
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An elected politician holds office while government is in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to crumple or tousle clothes or hair is to put them in disorder.

definitions.note: a phrase for a place, standing for a district within the capital

parts.note: to act is to play a part
on means continuing, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: An actor keeps performing in a London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only a location: the answer is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a district of west London, a place lying within the city.

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a test is a challenge
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch halts a duel by breaking into the challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something not moving is stationary, so having stopped means it is motionless.

clue.text: Go along with law restricting fungal growth

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the law word surrounds the other

parts.note: an act is a law passed by Parliament
a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a law that limits mould or mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to agree to or comply with something is to go along with it.

clue.text: Taxidermist initially given rotting body part

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: high meat or game is going off, starting to rot

explanation.surface: A taxidermist is handed a decaying piece of a carcass.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the upper part of the leg, between hip and knee.

clue.text: Giant mice to be dealt with? That's baffling!

indicators.note: cards dealt with are shuffled and sorted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Giant mice need handling, which is a puzzling state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something mysterious and hard to understand is puzzling or baffling.

indicators.note: placed in the other word, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
able means competent or proficient

explanation.surface: A footballer counts as skilled because of his goal-scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone made fit or permitted to do something has been qualified for it.

clue.text: Composure of bishop getting a puncture

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to lance a boil is to puncture it

explanation.surface: A bishop stays calm after getting a flat tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mental steadiness or poise, as in keeping one's balance under stress.

indicators.note: modified means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A metal gutter is altered to keep out rabbits.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'rabbit' is a hopeless batsman; such players bat last, at the bottom of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang: weak batsmen who come in last in the batting order are called rabbits.

clue.text: Get involved with priest's charity giving fruit trees

parts.note: to date someone is to get romantically involved with them
P is an abbreviation for priest
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Someone takes up with a priest's charity that hands out fruit trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: palms grown for their sweet brown fruit across the Middle East and North Africa.

clue.text: Holy man keeps Jerry in place

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the outer word holds the inner one

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a holy man
a jerry is British slang for a chamber pot, a po

explanation.surface: A holy man holds a German captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry' looks like the old slang for a German soldier, but here it is a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a particular location or site, as in 'a nice spot for a picnic'.

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking; the 's is read as 'is'
a booked seat is reserved

explanation.surface: A car park space has been kept on hold because it is booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something kept in its original state, like a well-kept building, has been looked after.

clue.text: Longs to inhabit street that's most exclusive

indicators.note: to inhabit a place is to live inside it, so this piece goes within

parts.note: wishes, as a verb, means longs or yearns

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to live on the poshest road in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: swish means smart and fashionable, so the superlative is the poshest.

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Dutch painting is showy and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective meaning showy; it is the verb to dart, move quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to move suddenly and quickly, as a fish darts or flashes across a pool.

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medic
over means finished or terminated

explanation.surface: A doctor sacked a labourer on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who herds livestock to market is an agricultural worker.

clue.text: An abstainer cut with stiletto when driving

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, same as a
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
to hew is to cut with an axe
a stiletto is a thin high heel

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is wounded with a dagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiletto' suggests a dagger, but it is the high heel of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a driver is said to be in this position, holding the steering wheel.

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Headlines report on a court case in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the most recent information or update, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

indicators.note: put into the other word, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a fish while swimming the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like the stretch of sea; it is a ditch or furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long narrow ditch dug in the ground is a channel or cutting.

parts.note: out means out of fashion, dated
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: Someone's dated haircut looks rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rock that shows above the surface of the ground is a rocky appearance.

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so T can stand for a model
an heir is someone who benefits from a will

explanation.surface: Someone's ideal heir is named in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: the plural possessive is used in place of 'his or her' for an unspecified person.

indicators.note: placed in the other word, so these pieces sit inside

parts.note: a camp is a faction or group, as is a sect
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A shady American parks in a holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something questionable or doubtful is not to be trusted.

definitions.meaning: one who shies, that is throws or pitches something

explanation.surface: A jumpier person is given the job of pitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: comparative of a word meaning timid, and a noun for someone who throws.

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was almost freed for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: without end, for all time.

definitions.meaning: hoists means heaves; the apostrophe drops the H, as a Cockney speaker would
the overhanging lower edges of a roof

explanation.surface: A Cockney hoists a section of roofing.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''oists' is the signal: the synonym heaves loses its H, as a Cockney drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: an H-dropping version of a verb for lifts, and the overhanging edges of a roof.

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a casket is a small chest
rated means marked or graded

explanation.surface: A golden casket was graded and given a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' suggests marks; it means arranged for an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: music written out or arranged for instruments has been scored.
